oliver: Notebook kernel hangs when calling AsyncClient from a top-level cell. Cell never returns, CPU spikes.

oliver: Minimal repro: 
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key='REDACTED')
resp = client.generate('hello')  # top-level cell, not awaited
print(resp)
```

priya: Jupyter runs an event loop; if you create an AsyncClient outside an async context and then call async methods without awaiting, things can misbehave. Do you see a coroutine object or a hang?

oliver: It hangs in httpx socket read (CTRL-C shows stack in httpx._client). If I `await client.generate('hello')` it works.

luke: Likely the transport isn't initialized until enter/await; also some notebook extensions import nest_asyncio which changes loop behavior. Workarounds: use `await`, use `async with AsyncClient(...)` in an await cell, or use the sync Client.

priya: UX fixes: add a notebook guide, a SyncClient wrapper using anyio.from_thread.run, and improve error messages when async methods are called from sync contexts. Filing issue #412.

luke: Draft PR #820 adds docs, a small `utils.ensure_async_started()` helper and tests that simulate IPython loop. CI started.

ci-bot: PR #820 checks started 551 https://ci.example.com/redwood/sdk/820

oliver: Typing nit: editors show generate() as Any. Please annotate AsyncClient.generate -> Awaitable[GenerateResponse]. Makes notebook DX better.

priya: Added typing task to #412. Action: priya -> docs notebook section, luke -> helper/tests, oliver -> verify on mac/linux kernels.

oliver: Verified PR branch locally; notebook hang resolved with examples. Will re-run in another kernel and report back.
